acceptance: Queue-time and merge-to-live statistics cover at least 30 days of production deploys after 2026-10-11, with the run ids used
A runner-pool decision with its reason is recorded in the D13 row of docs/internal/adr/adr-site-repo-split.md
context:
Found 2026-10-17 at site-split closeout: the follow-up list in site-split-99 names it, and no tracker item existed. Related but separate: actions-runner-queue-oracle-latency-20261009 (core CI queueing). Receipts come from `gh run download <run-id> -R BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site`.

Merged 2026-10-30 into actions-runner-queue-oracle-latency-20261009. On GitHub Free the site has no runner pool of its own: its jobs share the org's 20-job cap with core, so the D13 choice is the org-wide capacity decision. The D13 record requirement moved to that item.
description:
The site-repo split ADR (docs/internal/adr/adr-site-repo-split.md:33, decision D13) deferred the runner-pool choice: measure first, then decide after a month. Site receipts already record the inputs: queued_at, core_merged_at, live_at and core_merge_to_live_seconds (benchbox-site deploy/cli.ts:198-221, deploy/lib/receipt.ts:27-29). Nobody owns the decision, so it would otherwise be forgotten.

Collect the receipts of every production Deploy run from the cutover (2026-10-11, run 38177778939) to at least 2026-11-10. Report the queue-time and merge-to-live distributions (median, p90, max), then decide: keep GitHub-hosted runners, or move to another pool. Record the decision in the ADR's D13 row.
